These eight elements, summing to over 98% of the crust by weight, are, in order of decreasing abundance: oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, magnesium, calcium, sodium and potassium. However, non-silicate minerals are of great economic importance, especially as ores.  Non-silicate minerals are subdivided into several other classes by their dominant chemistry, which includes native elements, sulfides, halides, oxides and hydroxides, carbonates and nitrates, borates, sulfates, phosphates, and organic compounds.  Most non-silicate mineral species are rare (constituting in total 8% of the Earth's crust), although some are relatively common, such as calcite, pyrite, magnetite, and hematite.  There are two major structural styles observed in non-silicates: close-packing and silicate-like linked tetrahedra.  Close-packed structures are a way to densely pack atoms while minimizing interstitial space.  Hexagonal close-packing involves stacking layers where every other layer is the same ("ababab"), whereas cubic close-packing involves stacking groups of three layers ("abcabcabc")

Mount Everest.fact: In 1953, George Lowe (part of the expedition of Tenzing and Hillary) said that he saw bar-headed geese flying over Everest's summit.  Another bird species, the chough, have been spotted as high as the South Col at 7,906 m (25,938 ft) and yellow-billed choughs have been seen as high as 7,900 m (25,919 ft).  Yaks are often used to haul gear for Mount Everest climbs.  They can haul around 100 kg (220 pounds), have thick fur and large lungs.  Other animals in the region include the Himalayan tahr, which is sometimes the prey of the snow leopard.  The Himalayan black bear can be found up to about 4,300 metres (14,000 ft) and the red panda is also present in the region. Mount Fuji.question: It is located about _____ (62 mi) southwest of Tokyo, from which it is visible on clear days
Mount Fuji.fact: 24 m (12,389 ft 3 in).  It is the highest mountain in Japan, the second-highest volcano on any Asian island (after Mount Kerinci on the Indonesian island of Sumatra), and the seventh-highest peak of an island on Earth.  Mount Fuji last erupted from 1707 to 1708.  It is located about 100 km (62 mi) southwest of Tokyo, from which it is visible on clear days.  It has an exceptionally symmetrical cone, which is covered in snow for about five months of the year.  It is a Japanese cultural icon and is frequently depicted in art and photography, as well as visited by sightseers, hikers, and mountain climbers. Mount Fuji.subject: World Geography
Mount Fuji.question: The mountain is mentioned in _____ literature throughout the ages and is the subject of many poems
Mount Fuji.fact: It has been a frequent subject of Japanese art, especially after 1600, when Edo (now Tokyo) became the capital and people saw the mountain while traveling on the Tōkaidō road.  According to historian H.  Byron Earhart, "in medieval times it eventually came to be seen by Japanese as the "number one" mountain of the known world of the three countries of India, China, and Japan".  The mountain is mentioned in Japanese literature throughout the ages and is the subject of many poems.  The summit has been thought of as sacred since ancient times, and was therefore forbidden to women.  In 1872 the Japanese government issued an edict (May 4, 1872, Grand Council of State Edict 98) stating, "Any remaining practices of female exclusion on shrine and temple lands shall be immediately abolished, and mountain climbing for worship, etc. " Tatsu Takayama was the first woman on record to summit Mount Fuji in the fall of 1832

Mount Fuji.subject: World Geography
Mount Fuji.question: Approximately 100,000 years ago, "_____" was formed over the top of Komitake Fuji
Mount Fuji.fact: Scientists have identified four distinct phases of volcanic activity in the formation of Mount Fuji.  The first phase, called Sen-komitake, is composed of an andesite core deep within the mountain, discovered in 2004.  Sen-komitake was followed by the "Komitake Fuji", a basalt layer believed to have formed several hundred thousand years ago.  Approximately 100,000 years ago, "Old Fuji" was formed over the top of Komitake Fuji.  The modern, "New Fuji" is believed to have formed over the top of Old Fuji around 10,000 years ago.  Pre-Komitake started erupting in the Middle Pleistocene in an area seven km (4+1⁄2 mi) north of Mount Fuji.  After a relatively short pause, eruptions began again, which formed Komitake Volcano

Mount Fuji.subject: World Geography
Mount Fuji.question: Ashitaka Volcano was active from 400,000 to 100,000 years ago and is located _____ (12 mi) southeast of Mount Fuji
Mount Fuji.fact: Pre-Komitake started erupting in the Middle Pleistocene in an area seven km (4+1⁄2 mi) north of Mount Fuji.  After a relatively short pause, eruptions began again, which formed Komitake Volcano.  These eruptions ended 100,000 years ago.  Ashitaka Volcano was active from 400,000 to 100,000 years ago and is located 20 km (12 mi) southeast of Mount Fuji.  Mount Fuji started erupting 100,000 years ago, with Ko-Fuji (old-Fuji) forming 100,000 to 17,000 years ago, but it is now almost completely buried.  A large landslide on the southwest flank occurred about 18,000 years ago.  Shin-Fuji (new-Fuji) eruptions in the form of lava, lapilli, and volcanic ash have occurred between 17,000 and 8,000 years ago, between 7,000 and 3,500 years ago, and between 4,000 and 2,000 years ago

Mount Fuji.fact: Flank eruptions, mostly in the form of parasitic cinder cones, ceased in 1707.  The largest cone, Omuro-Yama, is one of more than 100 cones aligned NW-SE and NE-SW through the summit.  Fuji also has more than 70 lava tunnels and extensive lava tree molds.  Two large landslides are at the head of the Yoshida-Osawa and Osawa-Kuzure valleys.  As of December 2002, the volcano was classified as active with a low risk of eruption.  The last recorded eruption was the Hōei eruption which started on December 16, 1707 (Hōei 4, 23rd day of the 11th month), and ended about January 1, 1708 (Hōei 4, 9th day of the 12th month).  The eruption formed a new crater and a second peak, named Mount Hōei, halfway down its southeastern side

Mount Kilimanjaro.fact: Ice cores taken from Kilimanjaro's Northern Ice Field (NIF) indicates that the glaciers there have a basal age of about 11,700 years, although an analysis of ice taken in 2011 from exposed vertical cliffs in the NIF supports an age extending only to 800 years BP.  Higher precipitation rates at the beginning of the Holocene epoch (11,500 years BP) allowed the ice cap to reform.  The glaciers survived a widespread drought during a three century period beginning around 4,000 years BP.  In the late 1880s, the summit of Kibo was completely covered by an ice cap about 20 km2 (7. 7 mi2) in extent with outlet glaciers cascading down the western and southern slopes, and except for the inner cone, the entire caldera was buried.  Glacier ice also flowed through the Western Breach.  The slope glaciers retreated rapidly between 1912 and 1953, in response to a sudden shift in climate at the end of the 19th century that made them "drastically out of equilibrium", and more slowly thereafter

Mount Kilimanjaro.fact: One person in pictures or documents of the 1889 expedition was thought to match a living inhabitant of Marangu, Yohani Kinyala Lauwo.  Lauwo did not know his own age, nor remember Meyer or Purtscheller.  He did recall joining a Kilimanjaro expedition involving a Dutch doctor who lived near the mountain, and that he did not wear shoes during the climb.  Lauwo claimed that he had climbed the mountain three times before the beginning of World War I.  The committee concluded that he had been a member of Meyer's team and therefore must have been born around 1871.  Lauwo died on 10 May 1996, 107 years after the first ascent.  It is sometimes suggested that he was a co-first-ascendant of Kilimanjaro

Mount Kilimanjaro.fact: On the drier northern slopes olive, Croton-Calodendrum, Cassipourea, and Juniperus form forests in order of increasing altitude.  Between 3,100 m (10,200 ft) and 3,900 m (12,800 ft) lie Erica bush and heathlands, followed by Helichrysum, until 4,500 m (14,800 ft).  Neophytes have been observed, including Poa annua.  The lower northern and western slopes are dominated by Acacia savanna, while most of the wooded grassland of the lower southern and eastern slopes have been destroyed for cultivation.  Records from the Maundi crater at 2,780 m (9,120 ft) indicate that the vegetation of Kilimanjaro has varied over time.  Forest vegetation retreated during the Last Glacial Maximum and the ericaceous vegetation belt lowered by 1,500 m (4,900 ft) between 42,000 and 30,000 years ago because of the drier and colder conditions.  The Tussock Grassland is an area on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro that contains many unique species of vegetation, such as the water holding cabbage

In Tanzania, Kilimanjaro International Airport also serves as an important transportation hub. Mount Kilimanjaro.fact: Acclimatization is required, and even experienced and physically fit trekkers may suffer some degree of altitude sickness.  A study of people attempting to reach the summit of Kilimanjaro in July and August 2005 found that 61. 3 percent succeeded and 77 percent experienced acute mountain sickness (AMS).  A retrospective study of 917 persons who attempted to reach the summit via the Lemosho or Machame routes found that 70. 4 percent experienced AMS, defined in this study to be headache, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, or loss of appetite.  Kilimanjaro's summit is well above the altitude at which life-threatening high altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) or high altitude cerebral edema (HACE), the most severe forms of AMS, can occur.  These health risks are increased substantially by excessively fast climbing schedules motivated by high daily national park fees, busy holiday travel schedules, and the lack of permanent shelter on most routes

Mount St. Helens.fact: == Geology == Mount St.  Helens is part of the Cascades Volcanic Province, an arc-shaped band extending from southwestern British Columbia to Northern California, roughly parallel to the Pacific coastline.  Beneath the Cascade Volcanic Province, a dense oceanic plate sinks beneath the North American Plate; a process known as subduction in geology.  As the oceanic slab sinks deeper into the Earth's interior beneath the continental plate, high temperatures and pressures allow water molecules locked in the minerals of solid rock to escape.  The supercritical water rises into the pliable mantle above the subducting plate, causing some of the mantle to melt.  This newly formed magma ascends upward through the crust along a path of least resistance, both by way of fractures and faults as well as by melting wall rocks.  The addition of melted crust changes the geochemical composition

The modern period, since about 2500 BC, is called the "Spirit Lake Stage".  Collectively, the pre–Spirit Lake stages are known as the "ancestral stages".  The ancestral and modern stages differ primarily in the composition of the erupted lavas; ancestral lavas consisted of a characteristic mixture of dacite and andesite, while modern lava is very diverse (ranging from olivine basalt to andesite and dacite). Mount St. Helens.fact: Helens' eruptive cycles.  The Ape Canyon eruptive period ended around 35,000 years ago and was followed by 17,000 years of relative quiet.  Parts of this ancestral cone were fragmented and transported by glaciers 14,000–18,000 years ago during the last glacial period of the current ice age.  The second eruptive period, the Cougar Stage, started 20,000 years ago and lasted for 2,000 years.  Pyroclastic flows of hot pumice and ash along with dome growth occurred during this period.  Another 5,000 years of dormancy followed, only to be upset by the beginning of the Swift Creek eruptive period, typified by pyroclastic flows, dome growth and blanketing of the countryside with tephra. Since the late-1980s construction of the Sediment Retention Structure (SRS) on the North Fork Toutle River, coho and steelhead have been trapped and released above the sediment-capturing dam. Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: The _____ was Equipment to aids the traveler in navigation.
Navigational aid.fact: A navigational aid (NAVAID), also called aid to navigation (ATON), is any sort of signal, markers or guidance equipment which aids the traveller in navigation, usually nautical or aviation travel.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: The standards are defined by the _____ of Marine Aids to Navigation and Lighthouse Authorities (IALA)
Navigational aid.fact: The standards are defined by the International Association of Marine Aids to Navigation and Lighthouse Authorities (IALA).

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: IALA divides the world into two regions: A and B. Region B is the _____ (excluding Greenland) along with Japan, Korea and the Philippines
Navigational aid.fact: IALA divides the world into two regions: A and B. Region B is the Americas (excluding Greenland) along with Japan, Korea and the Philippines.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: In _____ region A where a minor channel branches off to port the mark at the junction would be a red cylinder with a green band
Navigational aid.fact: In IALA region A where a minor channel branches off to port the mark at the junction would be a red cylinder with a green band. In IALA region B the colours (but not shapes) are reversed.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: In _____ region B the colours (but not shapes) are reversed
Navigational aid.fact: In IALA region A where a minor channel branches off to port the mark at the junction would be a red cylinder with a green band. In IALA region B the colours (but not shapes) are reversed.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: There is no difference between _____ region A and B
Navigational aid.fact: There is no difference between IALA region A and B. The mark indicates a danger (shoal, rock, wreck etc.) which is isolated with safe water all around.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: On non-lateral markers, there are some shapes that show certain things: _____ show information, including places to find food, supplies, and repairs
Navigational aid.fact: On non-lateral markers, there are some shapes that show certain things: Squares show information, including places to find food, supplies, and repairs.

Navigational aid.question: This is known as a "synthetic _____"
Navigational aid.fact: AIS transmitted form an actual aid (buoy, lighthouse etc.) is termed a "real AIS AtoN". If it is impractical to equip the AtoN with an AIS transponder an AIS shore station can be assigned to transmit AIS messages on behalf of the AtoN.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography
Navigational aid.question: Each AIS AtoN must have a unique _____ (MMSI) number
Navigational aid.fact: Each AIS AtoN must have a unique Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI) number.

Navigational aid.subject: World Geography

Navigational aid.fact: In some cases, the lead marks/lights are provided by lasers, as in the laser channel under the Tasman Bridge on the Derwent River at Hobart, Tasmania.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: After the federal election of 1932, the party was the largest in the _____, holding 230 seats with 37.4 per cent of the popular vote
Nazi Germany.fact: After the federal election of 1932, the party was the largest in the Reichstag, holding 230 seats with 37.4 per cent of the popular vote.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The Reichstag Fire Decree, imposed on 28 _____ 1933, rescinded most civil liberties, including rights of assembly and freedom of the press
Nazi Germany.fact: On the night of 27 February 1933, the Reichstag building was set afire. The Reichstag Fire Decree, imposed on 28 February 1933, rescinded most civil liberties, including rights of assembly and freedom of the press.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 23 March 1933, the _____, an amendment to the Weimar Constitution, passed in the Reichstag by a vote of 444 to 94
Nazi Germany.fact: On 23 March 1933, the Enabling Act, an amendment to the Weimar Constitution, passed in the Reichstag by a vote of 444 to 94. The Enabling Act would subsequently serve as the legal foundation for the dictatorship the Nazis established.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 14 July 1933 Germany became a one-party state with the passage of the Law Against the Formation of Parties, decreeing the _____ to be the sole legal party in Germany
Nazi Germany.fact: On 14 July 1933 Germany became a one-party state with the passage of the Law Against the Formation of Parties, decreeing the Nazi Party to be the sole legal party in Germany. All civilian organisations had their leadership replaced with Nazi sympathisers or party members, and either merged with the Nazi Party or faced dissolution.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Further elections in _____ 1933, 1936 and 1938 were Nazi-controlled, with only members of the Party and a small number of independents elected
Nazi Germany.fact: Further elections in November 1933, 1936 and 1938 were Nazi-controlled, with only members of the Party and a small number of independents elected.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography

Nazi Germany.fact: The Nazi government declared a "Day of National Labour" for May Day 1933, and invited many trade union delegates to Berlin for celebrations.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Using deficit spending, public works projects were undertaken beginning in 1934, creating _____ new jobs by the end of that year alone
Nazi Germany.fact: Using deficit spending, public works projects were undertaken beginning in 1934, creating 1.7 million new jobs by the end of that year alone.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Up to 200 people were killed from 30 June to 2 July 1934 in an event that became known as the Night of the _____
Nazi Germany.fact: Up to 200 people were killed from 30 June to 2 July 1934 in an event that became called the Night of the Long Knives.

Nazi Germany.question: On 2 August 1934, _____ died
Nazi Germany.fact: On 2 August 1934, Hindenburg died. Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography

Nazi Germany.fact: The first major Nazi concentration camp, initially for political prisoners, was opened at Dachau in 1933.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography

Nazi Germany.fact: Beginning in April 1933, scores of measures defining the status of Jews and their rights were instituted.

Nazi Germany.question: These measures culminated in the establishment of the _____ of 1935, which stripped them of their basic rights
Nazi Germany.fact: These measures culminated in the establishment of the Nuremberg Laws of 1935, which stripped them of their basic rights.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The Saarland, which had been placed under League of _____ supervision for 15 years at the end of World War I, voted in January 1935 to become part of Germany
Nazi Germany.fact: When the other European powers failed to accept this offer, Hitler pulled Germany out of the World Disarmament Conference and the League of Nations in October, claiming its disarmament clauses were unfair if they applied only to Germany. The Saarland, which had been placed under League of Nations supervision for 15 years at the end of World War I, voted in January 1935 to become part of Germany.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In March 1935, _____ announced the creation of an air force, and that the Reichswehr would be increased to 550,000 men
Nazi Germany.fact: In 1934 Hitler told his military leaders that rearmament needed to be complete by 1942, as by then the German people would require more living space and resources, so Germany would have to start a war of conquest to obtain more territory. In March 1935, Hitler announced the creation of an air force, and that the Reichswehr would be increased to 550,000 men.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Britain agreed to Germany building a naval fleet with the signing of the Anglo-_____ on 18 June 1935
Nazi Germany.fact: Britain agreed to Germany building a naval fleet with the signing of the Anglo-German Naval Agreement on 18 June 1935.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Hitler sent military supplies and assistance to the Nationalist forces of _____ in the Spanish Civil War, which began in July 1936
Nazi Germany.fact: Hitler sent military supplies and assistance to the Nationalist forces of General Francisco Franco in the Spanish Civil War, which began in July 1936.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography

Nazi Germany.fact: The German Condor Legion included a range of aircraft and their crews, as well as a tank contingent. The aircraft of the Legion destroyed the city of Guernica in 1937.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Attempting to avoid war, _____ arranged a series of meetings, the result of which was the Munich Agreement, signed on 29 September 1938
Nazi Germany.fact: Attempting to avoid war, British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain arranged a series of meetings, the result of which was the Munich Agreement, signed on 29 September 1938.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In March 1939 _____ demanded the return of the Free City of Danzig and the Polish Corridor, a strip of land that separated East Prussia from the rest of Germany
Nazi Germany.fact: In March 1939 Hitler demanded the return of the Free City of Danzig and the Polish Corridor, a strip of land that separated East Prussia from the rest of Germany. Hitler, believing the British would not take action, ordered an invasion plan should be readied for September 1939.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Hitler, believing the _____ would not take action, ordered an invasion plan should be readied for September 1939
Nazi Germany.fact: The British announced they would come to the aid of Poland if it was attacked. Hitler, believing the British would not take action, ordered an invasion plan should be readied for September 1939.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop arranged in negotiations with the _____ a non-aggression pact, the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, signed in August 1939
Nazi Germany.fact: Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop arranged in negotiations with the Soviet Union a non-aggression pact, the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, signed in August 1939.

Nazi Germany.fact: Hungary was the fourth nation to join the Axis, signing the Tripartite Pact on 27 September 1940.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By late 1942 there were 24 divisions from Romania on the _____, 10 from Italy, and 10 from Hungary
Nazi Germany.fact: By late 1942 there were 24 divisions from Romania on the Eastern Front, 10 from Italy, and 10 from Hungary.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Germany assumed full control in France in 1942, Italy in 1943, and _____ in 1944
Nazi Germany.fact: By late 1942 there were 24 divisions from Romania on the Eastern Front, 10 from Italy, and 10 from Hungary. Germany assumed full control in France in 1942, Italy in 1943, and Hungary in 1944.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Using lists prepared in advance, some 65,000 _____ intelligentsia, noblemen, clergy, and teachers were murdered by the end of 1939 in an attempt to destroy Poland's identity as a nation
Nazi Germany.fact: Reinhard Heydrich, chief of the Sicherheitspolizei (SiPo; Security Police) and Sicherheitsdienst (SD; Security Service), ordered on 21 September that Polish Jews should be rounded up and concentrated into cities with good rail links. Using lists prepared in advance, some 65,000 Polish intelligentsia, noblemen, clergy, and teachers were murdered by the end of 1939 in an attempt to destroy Poland's identity as a nation.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Hitler's peace overtures to the new _____ were rejected in July 1940
Nazi Germany.fact: Hitler's peace overtures to the new British Prime Minister Winston Churchill were rejected in July 1940.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In February 1941 the _____ arrived in Libya to aid the Italians in the North African Campaign
Nazi Germany.fact: In February 1941 the German Afrika Korps arrived in Libya to aid the Italians in the North African Campaign.

Nazi Germany.fact: The Moscow offensive, which resumed in October 1941, ended disastrously in December.

Nazi Germany.question: On 7 _____ 1941 Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, Hawaii
Nazi Germany.fact: The Moscow offensive, which resumed in October 1941, ended disastrously in December. On 7 December 1941 Japan attacked Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The 1942 harvest was good, and food supplies remained adequate in _____
Nazi Germany.fact: The 1942 harvest was good, and food supplies remained adequate in Western Europe.

Nazi Germany.fact: In an attempt to resolve the shortage, in June 1942 Germany launched Fall Blau ("Case Blue"), an offensive against the Caucasian oilfields.

Nazi Germany.fact: Hitler's refusal to allow a retreat led to the deaths of 200,000 German and Romanian soldiers; of the 91,000 men who surrendered in the city on 31 January 1943, only 6,000 survivors returned to Germany after the war. Soviet forces continued to push westward after the failed German offensive at the Battle of Kursk in the summer of 1943.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By the end of 1943, the _____ had lost most of their eastern territorial gains
Nazi Germany.fact: By the end of 1943, the Germans had lost most of their eastern territorial gains.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In Egypt, _____'s Afrika Korps were defeated by British forces under Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery in October 1942
Nazi Germany.fact: In Egypt, Field Marshal Erwin Rommel's Afrika Korps were defeated by British forces under Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery in October 1942.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The Allies landed in _____ in July 1943 and were on the Italian peninsula by September
Nazi Germany.fact: The Allies landed in Sicily in July 1943 and were on the Italian peninsula by September.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By targeting oil refineries and factories, they crippled the _____ war effort by late 1944
Nazi Germany.fact: Many sorties were intentionally given civilian targets in an effort to destroy German morale. German aircraft production could not keep pace with losses, and without air cover the Allied bombing campaign became even more devastating.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 6 June 1944, _____, British, and Canadian forces established a front in France with the D-Day landings in Normandy
Nazi Germany.fact: On 6 June 1944, American, British, and Canadian forces set up a front in France with the D-Day landings in Normandy.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 20 July 1944, _____ survived an assassination attempt
Nazi Germany.fact: On 20 July 1944, Hitler survived an assassination attempt. Hitler's refusal to admit defeat and his insistence that the war be fought to the last man led to unnecessary death and destruction in the war's closing months.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Between 4 and 8 May 1945, most of the remaining _____ armed forces unconditionally surrendered
Nazi Germany.fact: Between 4 and 8 May 1945, most of the remaining German armed forces unconditionally surrendered. The German Instrument of Surrender was signed 8 May, marking the end of the Nazi regime and the end of World War II in Europe.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: High numbers of suicides took place in many other locations, including _____ (600 dead), Stolp in Pommern (1,000 dead), and Berlin, where at least 7,057 people committed suicide in 1945
Nazi Germany.fact: High numbers of suicides took place in many other locations, including Neubrandenburg (600 dead), Stolp in Pommern (1,000 dead), and Berlin, where at least 7,057 people committed suicide in 1945.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: A study by the historian Rüdiger Overmans puts the number of German military dead and missing at _____, including 900,000 men conscripted from outside of Germany's 1937 borders
Nazi Germany.fact: A study by the historian Rüdiger Overmans puts the number of German military dead and missing at 5.3 million, including 900,000 men conscripted from outside of Germany's 1937 borders.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Richard Overy estimated in 2014 that about 353,000 civilians were killed in _____ air raids
Nazi Germany.fact: Richard Overy estimated in 2014 that about 353,000 civilians were killed in Allied air raids.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Germany regained control of the _____ through a referendum held in 1935 and annexed Austria in the Anschluss of 1938
Nazi Germany.fact: The Saarland became a protectorate of France under the condition that its residents would later decide by referendum which country to join, and Poland became a separate nation and was given access to the sea by the creation of the Polish Corridor, which separated Prussia from the rest of Germany, while Danzig was made a free city. Germany regained control of the Saarland through a referendum held in 1935 and annexed Austria in the Anschluss of 1938.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany control of the _____, and they seized the remainder of Czechoslovakia six months later
Nazi Germany.fact: The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany control of the Sudetenland, and they seized the remainder of Czechoslovakia six months later.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Under threat of invasion by sea, _____ surrendered the Memel district in March 1939
Nazi Germany.fact: Under threat of invasion by sea, Lithuania surrendered the Memel district in March 1939.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Between 1939 and 1941, _____ forces invaded Poland, Denmark, Norway, France, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Belgium, Yugoslavia, Greece, and the Soviet Union
Nazi Germany.fact: Germany regained control of the Saarland through a referendum held in 1935 and annexed Austria in the Anschluss of 1938. The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany control of the Sudetenland, and they seized the remainder of Czechoslovakia six months later.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Germany annexed parts of northern _____ in April 1941, while Mussolini ceded Trieste, South Tyrol, and Istria to Germany in 1943
Nazi Germany.fact: Between 1939 and 1941, German forces invaded Poland, Denmark, Norway, France, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Belgium, Yugoslavia, Greece, and the Soviet Union. Germany annexed parts of northern Yugoslavia in April 1941, while Mussolini ceded Trieste, South Tyrol, and Istria to Germany in 1943.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Germany occupied the _____ protectorate of Albania and the Italian governorate of Montenegro in 1943 and installed a puppet government in occupied Serbia in 1941
Nazi Germany.fact: Germany occupied the Italian protectorate of Albania and the Italian governorate of Montenegro in 1943 and installed a puppet government in occupied Serbia in 1941.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By 1930 the Party won _____ of the federal vote, making it the Reichstag's second largest political party
Nazi Germany.fact: By 1930 the Party won 18.3% of the federal vote, making it the Reichstag's second largest political party.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: While in prison after the failed _____ of 1923, Hitler wrote Mein Kampf, which laid out his plan for transforming German society into one based on race
Nazi Germany.fact: While in prison after the failed Beer Hall Putsch of 1923, Hitler wrote Mein Kampf, which laid out his plan for transforming German society into one based on race.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Jewish civil servants lost their jobs in 1933, except for those who had seen military service in _____ of the Party or party supporters were appointed in their place
Nazi Germany.fact: Jewish civil servants lost their jobs in 1933, except for those who had seen military service in World War I. Members of the Party or party supporters were appointed in their place.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: As part of the process of _____, the Reich Local Government Law of 1935 abolished local elections, and mayors were appointed by the Ministry of the Interior
Nazi Germany.fact: As part of the process of Gleichschaltung, the Reich Local Government Law of 1935 abolished local elections, and mayors were appointed by the Ministry of the Interior.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: A new type of court, the _____ ("People's Court"), was established in 1934 to deal with political cases
Nazi Germany.fact: A new type of court, the Volksgerichtshof ("People's Court"), was set up in 1934 to deal with political cases.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In September 1935, the _____ were enacted
Nazi Germany.fact: In September 1935, the Nuremberg Laws were enacted.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: From 2 _____ 1934, members of the armed forces were required to pledge an oath of unconditional obedience to Hitler personally
Nazi Germany.fact: From 2 August 1934, members of the armed forces were required to pledge an oath of unconditional obedience to Hitler personally.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 8 July 1941 _____ announced that all Jews in the eastern conquered territories were to be regarded as partisans and gave the order for all male Jews between the ages of 15 and 45 to be shot
Nazi Germany.fact: On 8 July 1941 Heydrich announced that all Jews in the eastern conquered territories were to be regarded as partisans and gave the order for all male Jews between the ages of 15 and 45 to be shot.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Victories continued through mid-1940, but the failure to defeat _____ was the first major turning point in the war
Nazi Germany.fact: Victories continued through mid-1940, but the failure to defeat Britain was the first major turning point in the war.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The total number of soldiers who served in the Wehrmacht from 1935 to 1945 was around _____, of whom 5.3 million died
Nazi Germany.fact: The total number of soldiers who served in the Wehrmacht from 1935 to 1945 was around 18.2 million, of whom 5.3 million died.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Under Ernst Röhm's leadership the SA grew by 1934 to over half a million members—_____ including reserves—at a time when the regular army was still limited to 100,000 men by the Versailles Treaty
Nazi Germany.fact: Under Ernst Röhm's leadership the SA grew by 1934 to over half a million members—4.5 million including reserves—at a time when the regular army was still limited to 100,000 men by the Versailles Treaty.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Led by Reichsführer-SS _____ from 1929, the SS had over a quarter million members by 1938
Nazi Germany.fact: Led by Reichsführer-SS Heinrich Himmler from 1929, the SS had over a quarter million members by 1938.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: With recruitment and conscription based only on expansion, by 1943 the _____-SS could not longer claim to be an elite fighting force
Nazi Germany.fact: The Waffen-SS, the military branch of the SS, evolved into a second army. With recruitment and conscription based only on expansion, by 1943 the Waffen-SS could not longer claim to be an elite fighting force.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: From 1935 onward, the SS spearheaded the persecution of _____, who were rounded up into ghettos and concentration camps
Nazi Germany.fact: From 1935 onward, the SS spearheaded the persecution of Jews, who were rounded up into ghettos and concentration camps. With the outbreak of World War II, the SS Einsatzgruppen units followed the army into Poland and the Soviet Union, where from 1941 to 1945 they murdered more than two million people, including 1.3 million Jews.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: With the outbreak of World War II, the SS Einsatzgruppen units followed the army into Poland and the Soviet Union, where from 1941 to 1945 they murdered more than two million people, including _____ J
Nazi Germany.fact: With the outbreak of World War II, the SS Einsatzgruppen units followed the army into Poland and the Soviet Union, where from 1941 to 1945 they murdered more than two million people, including 1.3 million Jews.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In 1931 _____ organised an SS intelligence service which became known as the Sicherheitsdienst (SD; Security Service) under his deputy, Heydrich
Nazi Germany.fact: In 1931 Himmler organised an SS intelligence service which became called the Sicherheitsdienst (SD; Security Service) under his deputy, Heydrich. Himmler set up the beginnings of a parallel economy under the auspices of the SS Economy and Administration Head Office.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: The economist _____, President of the Reichsbank and Minister of Economics, created a scheme for deficit financing in May 1933
Nazi Germany.fact: The economist Hjalmar Schacht, President of the Reichsbank and Minister of Economics, created a scheme for deficit financing in May 1933.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In October 1933 the _____ was expropriated
Nazi Germany.fact: In October 1933 the Junkers Aircraft Works was expropriated.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By 1936, _____ regretted making the deal, as excess profits were by then being generated
Nazi Germany.fact: As the market was experiencing a glut and prices for petroleum were low, in 1933 the Nazi government made a profit-sharing agreement with IG Farben, guaranteeing them a 5 per cent return on capital invested in their synthetic oil plant at Leuna. By 1936, Farben regretted making the deal, as excess profits were by then being generated.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In another attempt to secure an adequate wartime supply of petroleum, Germany intimidated _____ into signing a trade agreement in March 1939
Nazi Germany.fact: In another attempt to secure an adequate wartime supply of petroleum, Germany intimidated Romania into signing a trade agreement in March 1939.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: A prototype was displayed at the _____ in Berlin on 17 February 1939
Nazi Germany.fact: A prototype was displayed at the International Motor Show in Berlin on 17 February 1939.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Six million people were unemployed when the _____ took power in 1933 and by 1937 there were fewer than a million
Nazi Germany.fact: The Nazi regime abolished the symbols of the Weimar Republic, including the black, red, and gold tricolour flag—and adopted reworked symbolism. Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: After the dissolution of the trade unions in May 1933, their funds were seized and their leadership arrested, including those who attempted to co-operate with the _____
Nazi Germany.fact: Six million people were unemployed when the Nazis took power in 1933 and by 1937 there were fewer than a million. After the dissolution of the trade unions in May 1933, their funds were seized and their leadership arrested, including those who attempted to co-operate with the Nazis.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: On 18 _____ 1936, Hitler named Göring as Plenipotentiary of the Four Year Plan, intended to speed up rearmament
Nazi Germany.fact: On 18 October 1936, Hitler named Göring as Plenipotentiary of the Four Year Plan, intended to speed up rearmament.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By January 1939, unemployment was down to 301,800 and it dropped to only 77,500 by _____
Nazi Germany.fact: By January 1939, unemployment was down to 301,800 and it dropped to only 77,500 by September.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: In 1942, after the death of _____, Hitler appointed Albert Speer as his replacement
Nazi Germany.fact: In 1942, after the death of Armaments Minister Fritz Todt, Hitler appointed Albert Speer as his replacement.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: By 1944, the war was consuming 75 per cent of Germany's gross domestic product, compared to 60 per cent in the _____ and 55 per cent in Britain
Nazi Germany.fact: The historian Richard Overy describes it as being somewhere in between the command economy of the Soviet Union and the capitalist system of the United States. By 1944, the war was consuming 75 per cent of Germany's gross domestic product, compared to 60 per cent in the Soviet Union and 55 per cent in Britain.

Nazi Germany.subject: World Geography
Nazi Germany.question: Germany imported and enslaved some 12 million people from 20 _____ countries to work in factories and on farms
Nazi Germany.fact: Germany imported and enslaved some 12 million people from 20 European countries to work in factories and on farms. Approximately 75 per cent were Eastern European.

Ocean.question: The photic zone starts at the surface and is defined to be "the depth at which light intensity is only _____ of the surface value" (approximately 200 m in the open ocean)
Ocean.fact: Human activity is mostly coastal with high negative impacts on marine life.  Vertically the pelagic zone is the open ocean's water column from the surface to the ocean floor.  The water column is further divided into zones based on depth and the amount of light present.  The photic zone starts at the surface and is defined to be "the depth at which light intensity is only 1% of the surface value" (approximately 200 m in the open ocean).  This is the zone where photosynthesis can occur.  In this process plants and microscopic algae (free-floating phytoplankton) use light, water, carbon dioxide, and nutrients to produce organic matter.  As a result, the photic zone is the most biodiverse and the source of the food supply which sustains most of the ocean ecosystem

Those currents are caused by forces operating on the water, such as temperature and salinity differences, atmospheric circulation (wind), and the Coriolis effect.  Tides create tidal currents, while wind and waves cause surface currents.  The Gulf Stream, Kuroshio Current, Agulhas Current and Antarctic Circumpolar Current are all major ocean currents. Ocean.fact: Salinity is higher in Earth's oceans where there is more evaporation and lower where there is more precipitation.
